newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ifo sees 97 German GDP growing at 2.0 to 2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Ifo sees 97 German GDP growing at 2.0 to 2.5 pct.

text.p: The Ifo economic research institute said on Thursday that it expected German gross domestic product to grow by between two and two and a half percent in 1997.
"All in all we expect a rise in real GDP of two to two and a half percent," Ifo President Karl-Heinrich Oppenlaender said in a speech prepared for Ifo's annual meeting,
Oppenlaender also said that the average number of unemployed in Germany would rise by over 300,000 to 4.3 million.
He said the average number of those in work would fall by 400,000 over the year.
Oppenlaender said, however, that in 1998 the number of employed would grow by around 100,000 from 1997 levels.
But, he said: "1998 average unemployment will still be 4.2 million."
For 1998 Oppenlaender said Ifo was forecasting economic growth of 2.75 percent, but said this forecast was on the upper end of the forecast range.

"In particular we have assumed (with this forecast) that European economic and monetary union (EMU), after Europe-wide savings measures, will start on time with a relatively large number of participants," Oppenlaender said.
